body.statement: Under the known uniform-design, polynomial-overlap, calibration-envelope, consistency, conditional-exchangeability, outcome-regression-law, and outcome-smoothness assumptions, the causal ATE equals the clean observed-law functional: \(\theta^{\mathrm F}(P^{\mathrm F})=\theta(P)=\int_{[0,1]^d}\{\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\}\,\mathrm dx\).
body.justification: This standard supporting result separates causal identification under the clean law from the contaminated-sampling decision problem.
body.gap: RosenbaumRubin1983 supplies the standard identification bridge, and the known uniform design converts the covariate expectation to the displayed Lebesgue integral; no novelty is claimed for this proposition.
body.consumer: The proposition lets applied ATE users interpret the statistical radius without asserting point identification of the clean law from \(R\).
